## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper needs a repeatable way to provision and rotate the Cloudflare Access service credentials used by crawl-remote consumers without mixing generations, exposing secret values through GitHub outputs, or coupling bootstrap authority to deployment authority.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a maintainer-only bootstrap workflow that reconciles one exact Access application and policy, publishes generation-bound pairs through short-lived repository-scoped GitHub App tokens, and resumes ambiguous rotations safely. The bootstrap and salted fingerprint remain dormant: this PR deliberately preserves the live `CRAWL_REMOTE_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN_SHA256` deployment contract until the slot-aware consumer and migration can land atomically.

## User Impact

Maintainers can stage or rotate crawl-remote Access credentials without manually coordinating partial secret writes. Existing production deployment behavior is unchanged, and cloud intake, publication, and slot consumers stay disabled until separate reviewed cutovers.

target.title: feat(gitcrawl): record digest-only evidence receipts
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/550
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/554
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/563

## What Problem This Solves

ClawSweeper can validate local and hosted Gitcrawl evidence, but operators cannot durably prove which snapshot, six-query results, coverage result, and parity result informed a later decision without retaining sensitive provider data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a bounded Evidence-family receipt API that records only canonical digests, finite counts, machine-safe snapshot/capability identifiers, and classified failure digests. It deliberately excludes raw rows, SQL, query arguments, prompts, logs, paths, tokens, bodies, intake activation, publication transactions, and GitHub mutation. Parity agreement remains distinct from coverage completeness. Failure fingerprints derive only from the already-published finite class, phase, and query identity, so raw error text cannot become a guess-verifiable oracle.

This draft is stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/554 so the receipt vocabulary follows the exact six-query, release-bound permanent-canary contracts. The cloud/parity intake consumer is https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/563.

## User Impact

Maintainers gain replayable audit evidence for hosted/local Gitcrawl observations without turning provider output or review logs into durable state.

## Evidence

- both TypeScript builds pass
- full focused ledger/receipt suite: 92 passed, 2 platform skips, 0 failed
- final focused replay/Gitcrawl rerun: 10 passed, 0 failed
- focused lint and format checks pass

target.title: fix(deploy): prove permanent Gitcrawl canary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A crawl-remote deployment can advertise Gitcrawl query support without proving that all six read-only query shapes work against deterministic data, that the live OpenClaw archive is fresh and complete, or that rolling propagation did not mix query responses from a predecessor release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Packages a checksum-pinned hidden canary seed into the immutable release artifact, seeds it only after exact deployment ownership and rollback-runtime proof, validates all six query envelopes and deterministic rows through the Access route, verifies fresh live coverage, and requires every query envelope to identify the exact deployed release. The permanent canary is intentionally retained across Worker rollback because the previously deployed runtime must declare canary support first.

## User Impact

Maintainers get deployment-time proof that hosted Gitcrawl queries are data-bearing, snapshot-consistent, release-consistent, hidden from archive listings, and backed by fresh complete live coverage before a crawl-remote release succeeds.

## Dependencies

- stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/550
- requires query-level release provenance from https://github.com/openclaw/crawl-remote/pull/40

## Evidence

target.title: fix(repair): preserve immutable retry inputs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where retry and self-heal dispatches could reconstruct repair jobs from mutable defaults or incomplete legacy artifacts, changing the original runner, mode, sandbox, model, or dry-run behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each repair attempt now records a bounded immutable input snapshot and retry paths recover the newest exact snapshot before considering durable or legacy fallback data. Recovery fails closed to plan-only, dry-run behavior when exact inputs are unavailable; historical final and worker artifact families remain supported without restoring the reverted action-lifecycle ledger or raw review-log machinery.

Self-heal recovery uses a shared three-minute scan deadline, so unavailable artifacts cannot consume the workflow's entire runtime budget.

## User Impact

Operators can requeue failed repair jobs without silently promoting permissions or changing the original execution inputs. Older runs remain recoverable through a narrow compatibility parser, while ambiguous or incomplete artifacts are rejected.

target.title: fix(ledger): preserve interrupted attempt mutations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupted repair execution could lose the mutation boundary entirely: current production emitted no `workflow.attempt` lifecycle, dangling `repair.execute` starts stayed open after crashes, and an earlier unknown outcome could override a later observed result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one narrow wrapper around the existing execute-fix command. It records bounded `workflow.attempt` and `repair.execute` start/outcome receipts, preserves the exact child exit or signal, terminalizes uncertain child receipts before the parent, folds outcomes by idempotency key and phase order, and publishes the finalized shards through the existing immutable state path. It does not restore the reverted PR 521 lifecycle or transaction modules.

## User Impact

Maintainers get production-backed interruption evidence for repair execution. Hard-killed mutation attempts fail closed, later observations supersede stale unknown state, retry evidence stays scoped to the exact workflow attempt, and the existing repair command remains the only GitHub mutation authority.

## Evidence

- focused/runtime tests: 147 total, 145 passed, 2 platform skips
